findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The query has no bound and `src/db.ts` `query()` returns `result.rows`, so the whole result is buffered. With the design's own figures (about 40 000 events per organization per month, kept seven years) one request materializes up to ~3.4 million row objects plus a CSV string of the same size in one Node.js process: memory grows linearly with the organization's history, and a few concurrent exports can exhaust the heap and crash the instance for every user. The spec requires every event, so do not add a LIMIT: read the rows in bounded batches (a server-side cursor such as `pg-cursor`/`pg-query-stream`, or keyset pagination on `(created_at, id)`) and stream each batch to the response, respecting backpressure. Select only the exported columns instead of `*`. Record the decision with its alternatives, since "none" were considered.
findings.title: The export loads the whole audit log of an organization into memory

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The design states the API runs "one event loop per instance". Formatting and joining millions of rows is synchronous CPU work proportional to the size of the log: while one administrator exports, every other request on that instance (including `/health`) waits, and the time grows with each month of retained events. Write the CSV incrementally — format each batch from the cursor and `res.write` it, awaiting `drain` — so the loop yields between batches; set `Content-Type: text/csv` with chunked transfer.
findings.title: Building the whole CSV with map/join blocks the event loop

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The schema of `audit_events` is not in the repository, so the index could not be checked. Verify with `EXPLAIN` that an index on `(org_id, created_at)` exists; otherwise the query scans and sorts a table that holds every organization's seven years of events. Keyset pagination (R-performance-1) also depends on that index.
findings.title: No index is stated for the org_id filter sorted by created_at

findings.evidence: **Alternatives considered**: none; the code is the simplest.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Measure the export on an organization with the full retention (memory peak, duration, event-loop delay) before choosing, and add a task that verifies the export of a large log stays within a stated memory and latency budget.
findings.title: The choice of the simplest approach is not backed by a measurement
